name: 2010 Château de Beaucastel Châteauneuf-du-Pape Hommage à Jacques Perrin
text:
## 2010 Château de Beaucastel Châteauneuf-du-Pape Hommage à Jacques Perrin

**The region and the estate.** Beaucastel lies at the northern end of the Châteauneuf-du-Pape appellation, near [Courthézon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Courthezon,+Vaucluse,+France&t=k). Here is the [estate itself](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Chateau+de+Beaucastel,+Courthezon,+France&t=k) and [Châteauneuf-du-Pape village](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Chateauneuf-du-Pape,+Vaucluse,+France&t=k). Records show a Pierre de Beaucastel buying a barn and land at Coudoulet in 1549, and that land still belongs to the estate. You can see [Coudoulet](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Coudoulet,+Courthezon,+France&t=k) from above too.

**The family.** Pierre Perrin, a son-in-law, later took over and greatly enlarged the vineyards, and the Perrin family has owned the property ever since. Jacques Perrin ran it until 1978, then his sons Jean-Pierre and François took over.

Jacques is the one who really put the estate on the map after the Second World War. In 1956 he converted Beaucastel to organic farming, when chemicals were the fashion, and he planted out-of-favour grapes such as Mourvèdre and Counoise.

**The wine.** Hommage à Jacques Perrin was first made in 1989 and is produced only in exceptional years. It is roughly 60% old-vine Mourvèdre, blended with Grenache, Syrah and Counoise, and aged in large casks (foudres). One merchant lists the 2010 as 60% Mourvèdre, 20% Grenache and 20% Syrah. About 500 cases of the 2010 were made.

**What the critics say.** Robert Parker gave the 2010 100 points in Wine Advocate issue 203, October 2012. That was the estate's fifth perfect Parker score for this wine, after the 1989, 1990, 1998 and 2007. His review is pure superlative; he essentially says he can't imagine what more a wine could offer.

Later tasters see it as a wine built for a long haul. A Waddingtons auction lot cites a Wine Advocate score of 98+, using Jeb Dunnuck's note. Dunnuck found it the most closed, dense and backward wine in the line-up, but with enormous potential. Nicolas Greinacher of Vinous scored it 98+ in August 2024. The German merchant Lobenberg rates it 100 and stresses its concentration and its closed character in youth.

Decanter's Christelle Guibert also tasted the 2010, but her score is behind Decanter's paywall, so I can't report it.

**Community notes.** I couldn't reach CellarTracker notes for this wine.

**Practical note.** At 16 years old, this wine is only now leaving its shut-down phase, given that Vinous still gave it a "+" in 2024. You can open it now, but there is no hurry, and most bottles should improve for another decade or more.

Stand the bottle upright for a day so the sediment settles. Then decant it for two to three hours. Serve it with Provençal beef daube, slow-roasted leg of lamb with garlic and rosemary, game birds, or anything with black truffle.

**Curious aside: heating the grapes.** Beaucastel uses a technique called vinification à chaud. The destemmed grapes are heated quickly when they arrive at the winery, which draws out colour and aroma and kills unwanted bacteria. They are then cooled. The estate also ferments Mourvèdre and Syrah, which are prone to reduction, in wooden tanks, while the grapes more prone to oxidation go into concrete.

**A second aside: Mourvèdre and "brett".** Beaucastel's wines have long been associated with Brettanomyces, a yeast that gives earthy, gamey aromas. Usually it counts as a fault, but it is typical of wines high in Mourvèdre. In an old Hommage, that savoury, leathery side is part of the appeal.

**From the history books**
- **1549:** Pierre de Beaucastel, from a Protestant family in Courthézon, bought the barn and land at Coudoulet. That was during the decades of tension that led to France's Wars of Religion. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Ch%C3%A2teau+de+Beaucastel&go=Go)
- **1956:** Jacques Perrin turned the estate organic and championed Mourvèdre, long before either was fashionable. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Mourv%C3%A8dre&go=Go)
- **1989:** The first Hommage à Jacques Perrin was made, and it earned 100 points from Parker. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape+AOC&go=Go)
